correctness.rationale: The exact powered-distance quadratic identity is expanded independently by distance class; blockwise orthogonal squares reduce it to one weighted Cauchy–Schwarz threshold. Strict monotonicity of each secular summand proves existence/uniqueness. Equality vectors, centered Gram rank, strict concavity/majorization, and the finite ordinary-p boundary enumeration are proved analytically. The standalone checker passed 6,570 supplementary assertions comparing independent graph shortest-path matrices and all projected eigenvalues; finite tests are not treated as proofs.

value.rationale: A clique of common vertices is a natural geometric replacement for a single universal hub. The exact classification reveals a qualitative core-size phase shift: fixed-size peripheral cliques with increasing number of blocks have critical exponent tending to log2(1+1/s)<1, unlike a one-hub bouquet. The precise partition extremizers and exactly five integer ordinary-negative-type boundary cases characterize a motivated graph-metric invariant, not arbitrary numerical samples; the critical null-vector gives geometric embedding-rank information. No paper-sized general theorem is claimed.
